The CIS program is recognized both regionally and nationally. Faculty have top academic credentials and industry experience and are committed to quality teaching and to working with students on relevant research that strengthens professional IT practice and teaching. In keeping with Cal Poly Pomona’s unique polytechnic approach to education, CIS students learn both theory and current practice in a strong, common core and in specialized courses. Using a hands-on, learn-by-doing approach, students apply cutting-edge technologies and problem-solving approaches to course projects and real-world problems. The result is graduates who are ready to excel in the technology-driven business world. The Department of Computer Information Systems fosters a culture of innovation, adaptability, and applied learning. The curriculum offers foundational and specialized coursework in cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, business intelligence, application development, and database management, all anchored in contemporary industry practice. Faculty bring extensive professional and research experience, ensuring that coursework aligns with evolving IT needs-such as cloud infrastructure, network security, and AI applications for productivity. courses.title: Introduction to Personal Computing
courses.description: Introduction to fundamental computer concepts and personal computing software through classroom and self-directed learning supported by interactive online learning environment. Topics include: Windows environment, word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, database, and computer concepts.

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Programming for Business Analytics
courses.description: Technology and programming foundation for business analytics projects. Python programming language in the context of business analysis.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 1200 or STA 1202 .

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Productivity
courses.description: Learn hands-on skills for leveraging cutting-edge AI tools across a range of productivity areas. Through guided exercises and real-world examples, explore generative AI applications and discover how to apply them effectively in business, content creation, project management, and beyond.

courses.title: Contemporary Operating Systems
courses.description: Introduction to contemporary computer operating system fundamentals. File Management, Virtual Memory, User Interface, and Device Management for Windows, OS-X, Linux, and UNIX operating systems. Virtualization of operating systems and processes.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1250 or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Cloud Infrastructure
courses.description: Exploration of IT infrastructure and its role in supporting and empowering organizations. Topics include telecommunications, service delivery, service level management, security, privacy, identity management, ethics and contemporary methodologies for managing IT infrastructure.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1250 or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming for Business
courses.description: Computer programming for business information systems. Object-oriented programming concepts, Java language, graphics, file operations, and Integrated Development Environment. Business application projects. AI-assisted programming.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1250 or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Database Design and Development
courses.description: Conceptual modeling, database design and implementation. Database inquiry and data analysis using a non-procedural programming language. Entity/Relationship diagrams, normalized database schema, structured query language. Distributed databases with integrity and security issues. Client server computing.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1250 or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming for Business
courses.description: Computer programming for business information systems. Object-oriented programming concepts, Java language, graphics, file operations, and Integrated Development Environment. Business application projects.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 1010 , CIS 101 or Personal Computer Proficiency; and C or better in STA 1200 or STA 120.

courses.title: Management Information Systems
courses.description: Introduction to the management and development of business information systems. Information systems topics include, competitive strategy, decision support, infrastructure, business processes, enterprise-wide systems, database management, data analytics, systems development and implementation, information security, ethics, and social impacts of information technology. Course concepts are supported with the use of business technology to develop problem solving skills.
courses.prerequisites: ACC 207 and 207A or ACC 2070 ; and CIS 101, CIS 1010 , or PCPT.

courses.title: Client-side Web Development
courses.description: Design and development of interactive and responsive websites using client-side technologies. Application of current HTML standards and multimedia elements for content. Use of modern CSS techniques for presentation style. Integration of JavaScript and JavaScript libraries for rich user experience and interactivity. Introduction to AI-assisted development.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 304 or CIS 2900 .

courses.title: Business Intelligence
courses.description: Data Science cycle, data acquisition, questions and ideal data set, data cleaning, data compliance and security, data sharing, data visualization, data modeling, data analysis and dissemination of results. Storytelling for intelligence dissemination. Differences and similarities among descriptive analytics, data mining, web analytics and big data. Artificial intelligence and data science. IT governance. Business intelligence, data reporting, digital dashboards. Using data modeling for decision making, business analytics. Industry cases in marketing, finance, manufacturing, human resources. Future trends of business intelligence. Ethical and privacy issues. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2100 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduction to artificial intelligence (AI) for business. Topics covered focus on AI technology fundamentals, including topics such as machine learning, deep learning and generative models, examines the diverse range of AI capabilities and applications in various business functions, and delves into the ethical and privacy issues of AI.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Location Analytics for Business
courses.description: Geographic Information System (GIS) and location analytics for business, spatial data type, spatial data analysis, spatial market analysis, location intelligence of business environment, solve location-based business problems, and ethical and legal aspects of spatial technologies and location data.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3252W and CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Data Warehousing
courses.description: Designing large databases using advanced data modeling concepts. Producing quality data models which follow corporate business plans, policies, and strategies of the enterprise. Extracting information from different data sources to create data warehouses. Design infocubes. Use in-memory databases. Strategic use of data warehouses. Ethics and privacy challenges.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 325 or CIS 3252W , and CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Telecommunication Networks
courses.description: Communication networks and the ability of such networks to address business needs. Topics include communications needs analysis, communication network design, software defined networking as well as implementation and testing networks.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2670 .

courses.title: Web and Mobile Analytics
courses.description: Web and mobile analytics studies the collection, analysis, and reporting of the audience, acquisition, behavior, and conversion data from websites and mobile applications, for the purposes of understanding and optimizing digital design, use, and performance. Advanced topics include data visualization, search engine optimization, attribution model, regular expression, tag management, conversion optimization, and the preparation for professional certification exams such as Google Analytics Individual Qualification (GAIQ) test.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3252W .

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Business
courses.description: Fundamental Artificial Intelligence concepts and methods. Techniques and tools in Artificial Intelligence for business. Practical Artificial Intelligence applications in Business. Artificial Intelligence projects.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2900 or CIS 2100 .

courses.title: E-Commerce Application Development
courses.description: Analysis of e-commerce architecture, practice, technology, and trends. Hands-on design and development of e-commerce solutions for modern digital market. Applications of online retailing, payment processing, data interexchange, search engine and social media optimization, and e-commerce security.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in the following: CIS 305 or CIS 3050 ; CIS 304, CIS 3050 , or CIS 3050 ; and CIS 311 or CIS 3110 .

courses.title: Server-side Web Development
courses.description: Development of web applications and projects for business using various server-side technologies, including Integrated Development Environment, web servers, and interactions with a database. Introduction to AI-assisted programming.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3050, CIS 2900 , and CIS 3110 .

courses.title: Secure Web Applications
courses.description: Identification of web application threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks. Analysis of major web application security risks in practice. Formulation of strategies with implementation plan for countermeasures for secured Web applications. Development of appropriate security mechanisms in the logic, coding, testing, and debugging of web applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in the following: CIS 305 or CIS 3050 ; and CIS 304, CIS 3090 , or CIS 2900 .

courses.title: Mobile Application Programming
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in mobile application development, Integrated Development Environment, business mobile application projects.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2900 .

courses.title: Information Systems Project Management and Development
courses.description: Application of Agile processes, methods, techniques and tools to develop information systems projects. Management of a comprehensive, team-based project development. Client partnership and user experience; team collaboration and communication; documentation and oral presentations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3110 and any of the following electives: CIS 4230, CIS 4250 , CIS 4260 , or CIS 4280 .

courses.title: Data Mining
courses.description: Data mining algorithms, machine learning to transform data into actionable knowledge. Business data mining projects.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3252W and CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Information Systems Auditing
courses.description: Fundamentals of Information Systems (IS) auditing. Understanding IS Audits, risk assessment and concepts, professional judgment, ethics, and techniques used in IS audits. Includes case studies on frameworks for the governance and management of enterprise IT. Explores the growing role of artificial intelligence in IS auditing, including its impact on IT risk assessment, controls, and ethical considerations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3050 and CIS 2900 .

courses.title: Internship in Information Systems
courses.description: Faculty supervised, on-the-job educational experiences in a real world IT environment. Allocation of credit is dependent on the nature of the work done and the number of hours worked. Students usually receive pay for participation. CIS 4410 and CIS 4420 may be taken four times each for a total credit of 16 units; with a maximum of 8 units per semester.
courses.prerequisites: CIS Major or Minor and Instructor permission.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total Credit limit is 16 units in CIS 4410 and CIS 4420; limited to 8 in total per semester.

courses.title: Internship in Information Systems
courses.description: Faculty supervised, on-the-job educational experiences in a real world data processing environment. Allocation of credit is dependent on the nature of the work done and the number of hours worked. Students usually receive pay for participation. CIS 4410 and CIS 4420 may be taken four times each for a total credit of 16 units; with a maximum of 8 units per semester. Allocation of credit is dependent on the nature of the work done and the number of hours worked. Students usually receive pay for participation.
courses.prerequisites: CIS Major or Minor.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total Credit limit is 16 units in CIS 4410 and CIS 4420; limited to 8 in total per semester.

courses.title: Big Data Analytics
courses.description: Concepts, techniques, and tools for big data analytics. Data analytics projects.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 2670 and CIS 4321 .

courses.title: Network Security
courses.description: Review of the fundamentals of network security in business environments with a focus on AI-enhanced cybersecurity. Topics include network security frameworks, measurement and mitigation of risk and best practices in applying security mechanisms from a business perspective. Apply AI-driven tools and automation to design resilient security strategies and evaluate compliance and incident response practices.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 2100 and a C or better in CIS 2670 .

courses.title: Natural Language Processing and Time Series Analysis with Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Explores cutting-edge techniques and algorithms in advanced data analytics, focusing on text mining and time series analysis. Leveraging trends in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Large Language Models (LLMs), and AI, to extract valuable insights from unstructured text, time series, and geographic data and make predictive analyses. Through hands-on projects, applications include advanced AI-driven analytics to real-world business scenarios, enhancing skills in managing, processing, and interpreting data for actionable business intelligence. Advanced algorithms, concepts, techniques, and skills in business analytics. Data analytics projects.
courses.when_offered: As needed; see Academic Department, Fall, Spring, Summer, Winter

courses.title: Information Security
courses.description: Introduction to computer security in networked systems. Security issues and policies with regard to hardware, software development, databases, operating systems and networks. Common attacks on systems will be covered. Vulnerability assessment tools and techniques for defending systems will be explored in various projects. Professional responsibilities.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 2100 , and a C or better in CIS 2650 or CIS 2670.

courses.title: Computer Forensics
courses.description: Computer forensics methodology. Legal issues regarding digital evidence seizure and chain of custody. Technical issues in acquiring computer evidence and analyzing data. Contemporary file systems are examined. Formal written reports and expert testimony.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3050 and CIS 2650 .
